answer: A strong anti-sybil pattern is binding identity to scarce physical cost. Every participant must post collateral, whether copper, compute or stake, before their votes count, so an attacker cannot spin up free identities the way a tide spins up foam. Misbehavior slashes the stake, while honest work compounds reputation like a walnut hardening its shell season after season. Faking many identities then costs real resources upfront, and the economy stays anchored to agents that actually produce value.
